# Data Collection

## Purpose

The purpose of the data collection stage is to assemble a documented
longitudinal evidence base for analysing Australian national research
computing demand and allocation.

The project draws primarily on publicly available NCMAS outcomes and
NCI and Pawsey reporting to identify historical requested compute,
allocated compute, resource type, Field of Research and other available
characteristics of national HPC activity [@HPCInternshipBrief].

Additional datasets, including research funding, workforce and research
activity indicators, are collected as potential structural drivers of
future HPC demand where sufficiently consistent time-series data are
available [@HPCInternshipBrief].

Because the availability, scope and definition of variables differ
substantially across years and sources, the purpose of this stage is not
to assume that all collected observations are directly comparable.
Instead, original values, units, reporting periods, source definitions
and data limitations are retained so that their suitability for
integration, standardisation and modelling can be assessed in subsequent
stages.

## Data Sources

Data was collected from several sources, including:

- National Computational Merit Allocation Scheme (NCMAS) outcomes and
  supporting documentation,
- National Computational Infrastructure (NCI) annual reports and
  publications,
- Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre annual reports and publications,
- Australian Research Council (ARC) funding data,
- National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) funding data,
- Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) data,
- research workforce and research activity data, and
- Field of Research (FoR) information.

International HPC data will also be considered where suitable data is
available, including information from EuroHPC, NSF ACCESS and ARCHER2.

## HPC Demand and Allocation Data

The main HPC dataset currently covers the period from 2013/14 to 2025/26.

The collected information includes, where available:

- requested compute,
- allocated compute,
- facility,
- HPC system,
- resource type,
- original compute unit,
- Field of Research,
- institution,
- source, and
- reporting period.

The level of detail varies across years because historical reporting
practices and available public information are not consistent throughout
the full period.

## Field of Research Data

Field of Research information was collected to examine how the composition
of HPC use has changed over time.

Where possible, historical FoR classifications are mapped to a consistent
classification to support comparison across years.

The available FoR data primarily describes the composition of allocated
compute. It should therefore not automatically be interpreted as the
composition of underlying research demand.

## Potential Demand Drivers

Additional datasets are being collected to investigate structural drivers
of HPC demand.

These include research funding, workforce, research activity and other
indicators that may be associated with changes in research compute
requirements.

The suitability of these variables for forecasting will be assessed later
based on their historical coverage, consistency and relationship with HPC
demand.

## Data Provenance

The original source, reporting period, reported unit and relevant notes are
retained wherever possible.

This allows subsequent transformations and assumptions to be traced back to
the original data source and helps identify observations that may not be
directly comparable across years.

## Data Collection Limitations

The main limitations identified during data collection include:

- limited consistent data before 2013,
- differences in reporting formats across years,
- inconsistent availability of requested and allocated compute,
- incomplete separation of CPU and GPU resources in some historical data,
- changes in HPC systems and accounting methods, and
- differences in FoR classifications over time.

These issues are addressed in the subsequent data integration,
standardisation and conversion stages.
